utterance: Good morning, Mr Mitchell. Your wife has brought you in today for some indigestion you've been having. Can you tell me more about it?
reply: It's like a heaviness. Like indigestion but heavier. Sort of a weight on my chest. It's been there an hour and a half, still there now. Right in the middle, behind the breastbone, bit up into the throat. Now you mention it, my jaw's a bit achy, and my left arm feels heavy. Not my back. Came on about seven this morning, over a few minutes.

awards.label: Whether the discomfort spreads or travels anywhere (arms, jaw, neck, back)

finding: Heart sounds dual, soft S4. No murmur. No rub.

utterance: Can you tell me more about the pain you're experiencing? Is it related to your breathing or movement?
reply: No, breathing doesn't change it. Moving doesn't change it either. Pressing on it would probably make it worse, but I haven't tried that.

awards.label: Whether the pain is worse on breathing in
Whether moving or pressing on the chest makes it worse

utterance: I'm going to get an ECG done to check your heart. Can you tell me if you've experienced anything like this before?
reply: This past week I've had a bit of tightness going up ladders. It goes away if I stop. I put it down to being unfit. It's been happening more.

awards.label: Red flag: Had this chest pain before, e.g. on stairs or exertion

result: Sinus bradycardia 54/min. ST elevation 2–3 mm in II, III and aVF. Reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. No LBBB.

utterance: Have you had any other symptoms like nausea or dizziness this morning?
Mr Mitchell, your symptoms and the ECG results suggest you are having a heart attack. I'm going to call an ambulance to get you to the hospital as quickly as possible for further treatment.
reply: I didn't think it was nothing serious. I just wanted some antacid.
